issues.title: crawl --sql returns empty extracted data due to UDF cache mismatch

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: browser4-cli crawl --seed-file urls.txt --depth 0 --sql @extract.sql --refresh

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Each crawled page's extracted data (title, price) appears in the result table/JSON.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: All extracted fields are empty strings. Pages are fetched (3 pages found, contentLength shown) but DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT in the X-SQL UDF returns no data unless pages were pre-loaded via goto+htmlsnapshot.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The H2 UDF backing DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT reads from the WebDB page cache, but crawl's internal session.load() does not populate that same cache. This is documented in project memory as Bug #2 (crawl-x-sql-bugs-2026-07-27). The CrawlToolExecutor may also drop sql/urls params (Bug #1).

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/api/controller/CrawlToolExecutor.kt

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Fix CrawlToolExecutor to preserve sql and urls params in CrawlRequest
- Ensure crawl session.load() populates the same WebDB cache that the X-SQL UDF reads from, or make DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT fall back to direct HTTP fetch when cache miss
- Add an integration test that verifies crawl --sql extraction returns non-empty data for a known page

issues.title: htmlsnapshot query results are inconsistent — same query returns data then 417 Expectation Failed

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. goto product page 2. htmlsnapshot 3. htmlsnapshot query with --sql @file — first attempt returns data with statusCode 200, second attempt returns statusCode 417 with resultSet:[]

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Consistent results for the same query against the same page.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: First query: statusCode 200, resultSet:[{title:'4K OLED TV 55',price:'$899.99'}]. Second query (after navigating away and back): statusCode 417 Expectation Failed, resultSet:[].

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Appears to be a cache-state dependent issue — the query succeeds when the page was freshly loaded by goto but fails on subsequent attempts. The htmlsnapshot command itself may evict or alter the cache entry. Needs investigation into how DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT resolves @url in the context of htmlsnapshot query vs crawl.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Investigate why DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT succeeds on first call but returns 417 on subsequent calls for the same URL
- Ensure htmlsnapshot capture does not interfere with subsequent htmlsnapshot query calls
- Add deterministic cache behavior so repeated queries produce consistent results

issues.title: MockSite fails to start from source due to missing MockServerPorts dependency

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./bin/test.ps1 mock-site on a fresh checkout

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: MockSite compiles and starts without manual intervention.

sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: pulsar-tests-common (which contains MockServerPorts) is a compile-scope dependency of browser4-rest-tests but is not auto-installed to the local Maven repo when building only browser4-rest-tests via test.ps1 mock-site.

sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add `-am` (also-make) flag or a pre-build step to Invoke-MockSiteBoot that ensures pulsar-tests-common is compiled and installed before building browser4-rest-tests
- Or add a `mvn install -pl browser4-tests/pulsar-tests-common -DskipTests` step to the mock-site launch sequence

issues.title: @ file path syntax causes PowerShell parser errors without quoting

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: browser4-cli crawl --sql @.test-sessions/extract.sql (without quotes in PowerShell)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The @file syntax is parsed correctly regardless of shell.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: PowerShell parser error: 'Unrecognized token in source text' at the @ character.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: In PowerShell, @ is a splatting operator. When an unquoted argument starts with @, pwsh tries to interpret it as a splat variable. This contradicts the SKILL.md recommendation to use --sql @file.sql for Windows.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Update SKILL.md shell-quoting documentation to warn about @ prefix in PowerShell specifically
- Document the quoting workaround: --sql "@path/to/file.sql"
- Consider supporting an alternative file-reference syntax that avoids shell-special characters (e.g. --sql-file path/to/file.sql)

issues.title: Crawl task list shows accumulated stale tasks with auto-cleanup message

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run crawl list after multiple crawl operations across sessions.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Clean task listing showing only current-session tasks, or clear separation of active vs historical tasks.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Shows 'Cleaned up 112 stale crawl task(s) — server no longer has them.' then lists 6+ tasks including ones from 12 hours ago. The auto-cleanup message is noisy and indicates the task store accumulates garbage.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The CLI's local task store retains completed tasks indefinitely. Stale tasks are only cleaned when the server reports they're gone (triggered by crawl list). No automatic TTL-based cleanup on the CLI side.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ (task tracking/listing logic)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a configurable TTL for local task tracking entries (e.g. 24h auto-expiry)
- Periodically prune completed tasks older than TTL without waiting for crawl list
- Show a less alarming message (or no message) for routine cleanup, and reserve warnings for actual errors
